utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you like to begin the cross-examination as soon as we get someone to cross-examine? MR. MEHMED ALIC, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you are still under oath, do you understand that, the same oath that you took yesterday? OK thank you. Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Alic, yesterday you told us that you saw Dusko Tadic with a man called Meakic one day when you were on the pista and you described him as being near the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In translation]: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that an occasion again when you were going to lunch in that building which had the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You remember indicating where you were on the pista and indicating as well where Mr. Tadic was with the man called Meakic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know then that Meakic was the Commander of the camp at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you may have to speak up just a little louder. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw the two men, was it just the two of them or were there others with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the two of them and around them there were guards around them all the time and they were walking around, but the two of them were sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they sitting on the ground or on a chair or a bench?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were chairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On this occasion when you were crossing the pista, were other men being held on the pista?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was on the pista, there were always people on the pista, inmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: To get to the restaurant building you go through the door in the middle of that building, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you with the men with you pass across the pista to get to that door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you mean? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you go through the men who were held on the pista in that group of 30 going to the restaurant to eat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were going -- the people were on the right and we were passing by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. As you told us, on these occasions you had to keep your head down, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So would it be right to say that the opportunity to look at the man Meakic and the man you said was Dusko Tadic was not a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was at the corner. I was the first in the line. I was always first when we went to lunch and so we were turning, we would turn our heads towards the wall, and when they said, "OK, it is over", then we would go and then I would just kind of glance over, you know, very fast, but you cannot look so, you had to keep going, but you were watched all the time from up there. He is looking around and he is watching who is turning and, you know, so we did not dare. We could not. So, they were beaten up, people, and they did not know they were being watched and then all of a sudden he would say, "You, come out here".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When you went out from the hangar to go to the restaurant building there were other guards around in the area watching you as well as the people on the pista, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The second time you told us that you saw Dusko Tadic with the man Meakic, that was on the other side of the restaurant building, the part of the model that is closest to you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was on the west side of the restaurant the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the other time it was the other side of the building, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the second time was on the east side of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Again, was that a similar occasion, were you going for lunch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the same situation, going to lunch, otherwise I could not see any because I was always in a room. Only when I was going to lunch, then that is when you see somebody, otherwise there are no other opportunities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the circumstances similar in that you were first in the line but you had to keep your head down and you were under the control of the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same, always the same, and always whenever I would go, I was -- that group that went, I was always the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you to went to lunch in this way did you walk or were forced to run as best as you could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we had to run but that is why they put me up front so that I am old, I was the oldest, and also my leg was not right, so I also pretended a bit more so that we could go slower, so I was always put up front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you ran as best as you could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As much as we could, how else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, it seems from what you are telling us that the circumstances of this second time were very similar to what you have told us about the first occasion, would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I noted yesterday that when you were talking about the surrender at Limenka, you said that you realised at that point that your freedom was taken away from you, and you were just to bow your head and that was it. I wondered if the expression "bow your head" was symbolic or literal. At Limenka were you required to look down to the ground or were you able to look around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were not asking that. They did not -- we did it ourselves so that we would not be recognised and so that they would not recognise us, and people knew my two sons. I had two sons and also the people knew me too, and I knew what was going on. So I was just looking in front, rather than being in a position when people would say, "Where are your sons?" So I was there and I was just not looking, because one of them, I had a daughter who is a deaf mute, and when we got off the bus they were looking through things and he was talking to her and she cannot understand him because she cannot hear him, and he did not know she cannot talk and then he says, "I will hit you with a rifle butt" and then I step in and I say, "She cannot talk" and he said, "Shut up or else I will hit you" and so I had to keep silent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At the time you saw Dule Tadic at Limenka you were looking ahead rather than looking down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right in front of me, I saw a few of them. You know, there is army all around, but if somebody would come that would recognise me, that would be, but it was not my goal to recognise people. My aim was to get saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Alic, please. Yesterday I believe you testified that at one point when you were in Omarska someone put a knife to your throat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At that time -- I do not have the transcript, but my notes at least tell me -- you did not look but you saw that Dule Tadic was there, was that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I testified in that way because I saw Dule Tadic before he recognised me, before they called me out, and he was there sitting with Meakic when we were going to lunch, and then I was called out "Mehmed Alic, called Meho", and a third is, they called out Alic Karabasic and Hrnic, those were the best three, the three best friends that were together, and then a fourth. When I was going out I heard them saying, "Dule don't, Dule, brother", and somebody says, "Mother" and that is why I claim, and that is why I took oath, that that is how it was and in my mind that is how it is.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So you did not see Dule when someone -- was Dule present when this person put the knife to your throat? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He -- of course he was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You believe that he was present because of the reasons that you have just testified to, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is sure, because he said, "What are you recognising, your mother?" and maybe it was 10, 15 per cent I glanced sideways and he says, "Are you recognising?" and then he put the knife, but I think that there was somebody else, somebody from Omarska or Prijedor there. He would not be interested in what I am looking at, what I am trying to recognise, but he knows that I know about Karabasic and I know Dule and I know all of them.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that Mr. Tadic put the knife to your throat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that with certainty, but he was in that group.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is one matter that I ought to raise with you. Yesterday when the witness gave evidence he did not say that he saw Dusko Tadic there in this incident that we are concerned with. He said, "I know he was there".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "There", and that was why I asked him the questions I did, to find out what he meant by "there", but if you wish to clarify that, you may ask more questions. It just seemed to me that when you say someone was there, it was not clear to me what the "there" meant, so you may ask more questions, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, you are the first witness to refer when looking at the model to north, south, east and west. Would you just clarify for me, am I right in thinking that that direction is north?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean, I was orientating myself on Bosnia. I knew in Bosnia what is north. I can show it here too. This is the west. This is south. This is north and that is east.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I am sorry, that direction is north? Would you point to north, the north direction in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Alic being permanently excused, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is not, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming today and yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thank you also for calling me and for allowing me to speak the truth. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. The next witness is Halid Mujkanovic. Before the witness enters, I should mention he was the subject of the most recent motion with respect to facial distortion.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then we may want to go into private session. Do not ask him, to go back. Then we need to, I think, close the blinds for him to enter and also, consistent with what we did with witness R, I believe we will have to put up the screens. Is that not so? We will then stand in recess for 10 minutes for that purpose. Thank you. (10.30 p.m.) (Adjourned for a short time)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before we proceed, we are hearing this witness in this manner pursuant to a motion filed by the Prosecutor which, I understand, has not been objected to by the Defence, is that correct? I thought I had granted permission when it was raised, whenever the Prosecution made that motion. If I did not grant it because it was not objected to, I am granting it now. Very good. An order will follow. MR. HALID MUJKANOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Please would you ask the witness to take the oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Sir, would you state your name please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am Halid Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What year were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 4th January 1965.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that where you were raised and lived until the time of the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you of Muslim background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you attend school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Elementary school, Rade Kondic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was your occupation before the conflict in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a cook. I worked in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since fifth grade of the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Since about the time you were in the fifth grade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Tadic well known in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because he had this karate school. He was a citizen of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see him frequently during the time you were a child attending school in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you continue to see him frequently as you grew up and became a young adult?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As a young adult, did you spend a lot of time in the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why was that? Doing what sorts of things? What was the purpose of being in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this was the centre, this was a meeting point. We met there and socialised around coffee pubs, coffee bars.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember when Mr. Tadic's cafe was built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was towards the end of '90.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see it being built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember who worked on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a lot of work there. There were many Muslims who worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Tadic's wife and who she was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mira, she was a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Over the many years during which you knew Mr. Tadic, is it fair to say that you saw him hundreds of times?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just raise one matter, your Honour? I think my learned friend is leading too much on this matter. It is a matter for the witness to say whether that frequency was appropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will sustain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, can you estimate the number of times that you saw Mr. Tadic over the years you knew him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot really try to calculate it, but numbers of times, sometimes several times a day, sometimes several times a month, but I really cannot say, to say 100 times or 200 times. I used to see him very often, very many times since he was a known person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not Mr. Tadic had a noticeable or characteristic way of walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Why, he had his characteristic gait. He walked, he made a kind of a movement which I think he had since birth, I mean, how he walked, at any rate, his walk, yes, he was quite characteristic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Emir Karabasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Jasko Hrnic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know Enver Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Dule Tadic know those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At different times did you see him with one or the other of those persons in cafes or in the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the attack on Kozarac began on May 24th were you in Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you spend the first two nights of the attack in the area of a nearby creek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, near my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On Monday, the second day of the attack, did you spend time at a neighbour's house where some members of your family were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also go to your home in an attempt to free your livestock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On Tuesday, the third day of the attack, did you surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you do so with a few people including the Imam of your local mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did you first surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I surrendered on the main road in Kozarusa. The main road is between Prijedor and Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you surrender to members of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you surrendered, were you then taken along with the others in the direction of Kozarusa to the area where the restaurant Ziko was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far was that from where you had first surrendered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What time of day was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the morning, around 10 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there Serb forces at the area of Ziko's restaurant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there buses there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the buses have people on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were full.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was on those buses, men, women, children, who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those buses where I surrendered one kilometre away were full of women and children and at Ziko's they were all men, male.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What nationality were those women and children on the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain at the area of Ziko's restaurant or were you taken elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they put us on the buses straightaway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did the buses go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor. First, the buses with women turned off towards Trnopolje and the ones with men went to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Keraterm where were you held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a large room, I do not know how they called it. I think maybe it was No. 2 but it was a large room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you spend that night in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, I could not hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you spend that night in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The following night were you transferred from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After you arrived in Omarska where did you spend the first night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent it in a room which was with within, where was -- where the kitchen was. Upstairs there were interrogating rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long were you held in the room in the kitchen building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed about two days and then the interrogation started, and I was one of the first to go to interrogation. Then I was moved to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Into which room in the hangar were you placed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The room that had the glass door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After one entered the glass door and continued toward the back of the room, what would be there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On both sides there was a hallway and a staircase leading up to the room. On both sides there were lockers where you could leave your clothes, so there were metal lockers. There was nobody there. I was the first one to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have this photograph marked as Exhibit 260 for identification, please? That photograph is marked as 19/24 and it can be called up on the screen with that designation. Mr. Mujkanovic, do you recognise what is shown in this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that is where I was, in this corner, but there are no lockers here on the two sides. I was here on top of the locker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, I would tender this photograph for admission.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 260 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could have it placed on the Elmo? Perhaps the witness can indicate again where his place in the locker was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The lockers were here on one side and the other side here. I was here on the locker.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you remain held in that room until you were transferred to Manjaca in August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, how would you describe the general conditions in Omarska during the time you were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you can call them conditions, those were terrible conditions, hunger and then scabies, lice, dysentery. I do not know what else to mention. I do not know -- impossible conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners regularly beaten on their way to lunch or going to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners also singled out for individual or special beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you singled out for an individual or special beating while you were in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who called you out for that beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They called him "Bakar". He had a scar on his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Approximately, when was it that he called you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but I think towards the end of July. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where did he take you after he called you out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took me to a room -- as you enter the hangar, there was a small room immediately to the right which was -- there were a few lockers there and then a small table. When he brought me to that room, he asked money from me, and I told him I did not have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry, how much money did he ask for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 20 billion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 20 billion of what currency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just to put that in perspective, was that a time when it look millions of dinars to buy the simplest of items?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What happened after you told Bakar that you did not have the money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said to lean over the table and then he started beating me with a cable. It was a thick cable and it hurt a lot. He kept beating me. When I fell off the table, he hit me a few more times and told me that I had 10 minutes to bring him those 20 billion dinars. I went back and I asked around. I knew that all of us were pretty much in the same position. Everything had been taken away from us. Then he took me back to the same room and asked me if I had brought him the money, and I told him I did not have any and then I had to do the same thing over the table, and then again he beat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How long did that beating last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, long because it hurt a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did Bakar tell you when he stopped beating you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said, "Tomorrow night I am coming back to my shift". I had to give him 30 billions or else he was going to kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you make an effort again to locate or come up with some money to satisfy his demand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I asked, I begged from people, and from all of that I got a Seiko watch that was five billion and a small silver chain. When he came back to his shift, he called me immediately to that same room and asked me if I had found the money for him. At the same moment I brought out of my pocket everything that I had. He hit me a few times and said to run. Then I left the room. Another soldier came by and hit me with a rifle butt on my chest and I fell down. He started to hit me with his boots and he stepped on my head and squeezed my ear, hit me in the stomach and he hit my intestines and then the other one said, I beat him enough, leave him alone. Then they cursed my mother and told me to leave. I do not know how I ran to the room where I was. I fell down and I could only say "water".

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was this guard who was striking you with his feet, kicking you or stomping you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kicking and stomping.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How hard did he kick or stomp you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that my colon protruded out and he smashed my ear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, during the time you were in Omarska did you see Dule Tadic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there in my room by the lockers next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know when that occurred? What date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The exact date, I do not know. I do not know if it was June or July, but it was afternoon when it ----

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were prisoners called from rooms in your area that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was first called from your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, it was Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was Emir Karabasic held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the same room but he was on the top floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So he was upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you notice who called him out or did you know the person who called him out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the person who called him out a regular guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What did that person say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He called him out and he told him that he had a minute to get down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you aware of what Emir's physical condition was before that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten up a few days earlier, so he was recovering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Emir Karabasic come down in response to the soldier ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I did not ask you, what was the person who called him out wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When Emir came down did that soldier say anything to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he hit him and he cursed his balija mother. He said, "Why are you dragging?" because he was moving too slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After Emir Karabasic left the room, did you hear anything coming from the area of the hangar floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, screams and cries.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that for a short time or did that continue for some time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot determine, to me it was long, but I do not know how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was someone else called from the room after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Eno Alic was called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Eno Alic respond immediately after he was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was someone else sent to get him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, his father, Meho Alic, came.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did a soldier bring Meho Alic to the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did Meho Alic go upstairs to look for his son?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After some time did you see them both come down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After the two of them left the room did you hear what was happening outside?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard what was happening -- again cries and screams and so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did prisoners in your room do anything after these screams and cries had begun and were continuing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, many of them ran upstairs to the top floor. I only managed to jump off the locker to the corner next to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Why did you jump off the locker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wanted to run away like the others, but I did not manage because it was so -- the regular guards were so close looking at me, if I did run maybe they would get me, they would call me out to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What position did you take after you jumped off the locker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the corner there was, I do not know, there was either a dress or something. I was in some kind of crouching, kneeling position and my hands were up like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what you were sitting on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was something there. There were some clothes or maybe there was something underneath. I do not know exactly. There was something. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were other prisoners called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who else did you hear called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic was called out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know where his room was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His room was next to mine, the next one over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Jasko Hrnic called out more than once?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When he finally responded to the calling out, did he pass by the area of your door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to see his face or the face of any guard he was with as he started walking by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw his face when the guard was escorting him. When he was hit by the guard passing by the door and when he bent over, I saw his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know what Jasko's condition had been before this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was also recovering. He had been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than the three persons you have mentioned, that is, Emir Karabasic, Eno Alic and Jasko Hrnic, did you hear any other prisoners called out during the approximate time of this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I heard, I personally heard Beganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that coming from the area in front of your door or from some other portion of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was approximately around the toilet. That is where it came from. That is where I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The sounds of beating or the sounds of crying and screaming which you stated before, were they continuing after Jasko Hrnic was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did those cries and screams continue for a brief time or continue for a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For me, it lasted a long time. I do not know how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As you continued crouching in the corner, were other prisoners taken from your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they called out by name or selected in some other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they said two volunteers must come out, if they do not come out they would kill somebody. Across from me there were two men and they came out and went over to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Using initials, can you tell us who those men were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was G and H.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After G and H were called out, did you hear more screams and cries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have described the position you took in the corner and how you had your hands over your face in an effort to signal to the guards outside that you were not looking. Did you, nevertheless, look at certain times during the incident to see what was happening outside the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you watch the entire incident or only portions of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you know how much time passed between those portions of the incident when you were watching and those portions when you were not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is hard for me to estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you then to tell us what you did see during those times that you were looking out from your room on to the floor of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw when G was coming out of the canal, he was all covered in oil.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Had you heard any shouting or words coming from the area of that canal ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- shortly before he came out, and what did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A pig, like pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What else were you able to see, Mr. Mujkanovic, during those times you were looking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw when H was holding, I cannot quite say whether it was Emir Karabasic or somebody else, by the hands, when he was holding him by the hands, G had to bow down in his crutch and it was ordered to him that he must bite the genital. When I looked up the second time, in those moments there were screams. When the second time I looked, G got up with his mouth full. He was all bloody from oil. Those moments that there was a group of soldiers, somebody was shooting up in the air, and a little time passed. One of the soldiers brought him to this person, a dove to this person which was lying on the concrete and he was given this dove or pigeon that was still alive and was given to this person to eat. The second time I looked, Jasko Hrnic was not far from me and a soldier beat him with, I do not know what it was, a metal iron bar or something, but as he fell he was showing no signs of life, and music was played, "Let me live" was the name of the song. It was hard for me. My stomach was churning. I do not know how I ran away upstairs to the toilet, which was upstairs when you got upstairs to the left. How I got there to the toilet, I do not know, to throw up even though I had nothing to throw up. I did not eat anything. I had not eaten anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see many soldiers on the hangar floor during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were there, I do not know how many, but a group of them, as far as I could see, I do not know how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were they always together or were they in separate groups at times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those that I saw were in a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How were these soldiers acting? What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they looked as if they were attending a sports match, as if they were supporting a team.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you see Dule Tadic during this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I object, your Honour? Perhaps the appropriate question (because, in my submission, this is a leading form) would be to ask the witness whether he recognised anyone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Rephrase the question. MR. TIEGER (To the witness): Mr. Mujkanovic, during this incident did you see anyone in the hangar whom you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Where was he when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I saw him he was on a tyre and the second time he was on the concrete in front, by one of the canals which was across the WC, facing towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to stand up for a moment and using that pointer show us on the model where Dule Tadic was those two times you saw him during the incident? If I can remind you to rise slowly and move slowly because of the camera? Mr. Mujkanovic, I am told you need to go back to your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go back to your seat, this way. What we will do is pull a few of the blinds down. Perhaps the two blinds next to the screens can be lowered? Would that help, Mr. Tieger? Mr. Kay, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Mujkanovic, if I could now ask you again to rise slowly from your chair and go to the model and show us the approximate area where Dule Tadic was when you saw him those times.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you need to approach, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time he was here and the second time here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: The second time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I am sorry. Can you show us the approximate areas again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time here the second time here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In what direction was Dule Tadic facing on those two occasions you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers around him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if you would get the witness also to point out where he was?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you to rise again and show us your room and where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was here, he was here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There are some blue numbers there, are there not, nearby? Will that help to show more -- go ahead, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sir, if there is a number which appears on the floor of the room in which you were, if you could read that number for us?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be switched on for the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you see a number written on the floor of the room in which you were held?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You can resume your seat. Mr. Mujkanovic, do you see Dule Tadic in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he is wearing, please, so we can identify that for the record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He has a suit of a sort of a green colour. He has a tie. He also has an off-white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What was Dule Tadic wearing when you saw him on the hangar floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On that day do you recall whether he was clean shaven or had a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, a few days growth. It was not long, it was not short, well, sort of a couple of days, two or three days growth, I would not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, first may the record reflect the identification of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will reflect that the witness identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (11.38 a.m.) (Adjourned for a short time) (12.00 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Mujkanovic, did you know Emir Karabasic before you were detained in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Eno Alic, did you know him before you were detained in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Jasko Hrnic, did you know him before you were detained in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area where you were confined, you have told us, was in this room or hallway at the foot of the stairs, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you were not staying in a room on the floor above?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was in the corridor and there were the stairs which led upstairs of that same room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The place in the corridor became your room whilst you were staying in Omarska, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The room above was a room where there were many prisoners detained, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The room where you were detained, did it have guards separate from those who would have been guarding the room above?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The door which was a glass door into the hangar, was that a door that was generally closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One wing was open, a part of the door. A part of the door was open, the central part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The incident that you have been describing as happening concerning Karabasic, Alic, Hrnic, on that occasion was that door to the hangar closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Open, it was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you stayed down there and it was your room, about how many other people were in that area like you staying there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know about myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, were you in this place then on your own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that place where I was, I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was your place there on your own the whole time that you were staying there in that part of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Throughout my stay in the camp I was on the locker, and that was in the corner when you come down from the locker on the tiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have shown us that in the photograph, and ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- the place where you slept then, was that on top of the lockers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Other people were not staying down there with you, it was just you on your own, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When? At that moment or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asking about the whole period of the time that you were in that place in the camp, in that hallway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, at that time it was full, both down and on the lockers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the day of this incident that you have been telling us about, did the other people who stayed in that part of the hallway remain there or did they leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They left, escaped, upstairs, up the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they escape before anyone was called out by the guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At what stage did they leave that hallway to go upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said it once and I shall repeat it. When Eno Alic was taken away, then they left, went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that the guards asked for two volunteers to come out, and those are the men you have described as G and H. At what stage were they asked to be volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Eno Alic and Emir Karabasic were taken out, volunteers who were -- had to volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When those two were selected, had the others left that hallway by then, or did they leave after those two had been selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already said, they left after Eno Alic was taken away. Some of them, those two across me who stayed, they went out as volunteers without choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So after they had gone and the others were left, were you the only person remaining in this part of the hallway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that I was there on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It seems then that the guards allowed the other people to leave that part of the hallway and go upstairs to another room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How were the other people who had previously been staying then in this part of the hallway able to leave that area and move elsewhere in the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They should know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that you did not feel it was possible for you to escape from the area because of the guards that were there, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "because of those guards that were there", how many guards do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell me where they were positioned in relation to that part of the hallway where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not far from me, by my side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So they were in the area of the hall, were they, rather than being in the actual hangar part of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, they were the other side of the doors that you have referred to as opening from the hallway into the hangar, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, outside the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there any guards that you knew of who were in the area above this part of the hallway, in the room above or in the hallway above or at the top of the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards did not go in there. There were people, Muslims, shut up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So there were no guards stationed up there in a position standing outside any room where Muslim men were detained, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said they were in front of it, in the hangar, not far from the area, from the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, why was it then that you did not leave this part of the hallway and, like the others, go upstairs to a room there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I did not manage to flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But it seems that there was nothing to have stopped you from moving there once the guards had selected their two volunteers to go into the hangar, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, I am asking you to see if you can help me on this because I am interested to know how it is you remained in this area on your own.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it was all full, narrow staircase, who managed to escape upstairs, he did, and since I was on the locker I managed to jump down and I stayed in that corner in that posture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you jumped down, was that after the two volunteers had been selected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was already down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you jumped down to the posture that you told us about, was that because you were hiding from the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what was then, I know I simply remained. I kept that posture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It seems then that you thought it was better to try to conceal yourself rather than stand up and be noticed, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As you told us, you covered your eyes with your hands so that no one would believe you were watching what was happening in the hangar, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but my hands were like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you lying down on the floor looking through the glass of the door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that I was neither sitting nor crouching in that posture. It was something, it was clothes or something, I do not know what it was, it was something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The doors that you have mentioned are doors that have a glass section, is that right, and beneath that a metal section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door was all glass, only the frame was metal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you telling us then that it was glass from the top of the door down to the bottom of the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was about 20 centimetres of this metal frame all around, and at the bottom all the rest was glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could look at Exhibit 260 which was shown to us earlier today? Perhaps if it could be put on the overhead projector so that everyone can see it? It is actually on the video monitor, Mr. Bos, so there is no need. Thank you very much. (To the witness): You can see the photograph, Mr. Mujkanovic, that is in front of you now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see here the glass that is within these doors and the panels on the side, and beneath that a metal bottom. Just looking at this photograph, can you indicate to us which side on the photograph you would have been looking through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would just describe it, if it is on the left side as we look at the photograph, or right side, or which of the panels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you enter that room, that corridor, it is the left side. If you go out of it, then it is to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it that side panel beside the door itself which was the part of the glass that you were looking through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that this is the glass through which I looked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am asked to indicate that on the Elmo so that it is without any doubt. If you could just use that pointer and point to the photograph on the monitor and then we can see? So it is that second panel from the left, is that right? Thank you. The hangar that you were looking out into was a hangar which had equipment within it such as trucks, other items connected with the ordinary use of that building, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once upon a time, at that time in this area which I faced, it was the same, as far as I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area that you were looking into in the hangar was not an area that was lit by any artificial lighting, is that right? I am sorry, I did not catch the translation of that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry we did not hear the reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps could you reply and the second microphone be switched on for the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may have to repeat the question for the witness, if you will?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. (To the witness): This building called the hangar that you were looking into was not lit by any artificial lighting, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During day time it was lit because the door was open, the door of the garage was open -- it was a big door -- so that there was enough light to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On this occasion, though, was that door to the garage open or was it closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes it was open and sometimes it was closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it closed on this occasion when this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the visibility was all right, it was day time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you are inside a large building and you are not outside in the daylight. What I am asking about is the lighting conditions within this part of the building.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a fair answer, Mr. Mujkanovic, or an answer that you are just giving because you believe it helps what you have told the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the visibility was all right and there was light.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area that you were looking into contained a number of men who have been described as soldiers. Did you recognise anyone else there out in the hangar when these incidents were happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised Dule Tadic. He was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you did not recognise anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The number of men that we are talking about as being in the hangar at this time, soldiers who were part of this group, is how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, a group, how large were the group I saw, seven or 10, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you cannot give any names of those people, did you know any of them in any other way, recognise them in any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What people? The soldiers or?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The soldiers whom I am asking you about at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it the case then that you are giving Dule Tadic's name because that is a name that has been given to you by someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not given it. I saw him with my own eyes because I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know a Miso Danicic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Could I have that Exhibit again, that photograph? (Handed) Witness, would you turn round and face me? Thank you. This photograph that you have seen, that is taken from the floor of the hangar looking towards the stairs, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where did the volunteers come from? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were across the room from me. They were also sitting down on the tiles.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So they were not upstairs, they were on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: These soldiers that you saw in the hangar, had you ever seen any of them other than the man you say was Dule Tadic before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So they were not regular visitors who came to deal with the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you saw Mr. Tadic and he was facing towards you, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How far away was he from where this incident was taking place that you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Close. I could not say it really down to a centimetre, but not too far.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You have indicated you could not estimate the number of, did you say centimetres that Mr. Tadic was from where this incident was taking place, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Tadic involve himself at all in the incident that was taking place, and by "involve" I mean take an active part, and that may mean even -- pardon me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see those moments.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So you did not then see Mr. Tadic require any of, Mr. G for example, to commit the acts that you have described, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. We will leave the courtroom and adjourn early for lunch, it is suggested, so that arrangements can be made for the next witness. Sir, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming. We will leave and then you may leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. We will stand in recess for an hour and a half. I do want to be available to work with the lawyers if you need any assistance in making the arrangements for the next witness. I have asked the Registry to see if we can locate another piece of equipment which might help. So if you will just remain a few moments and we will see what can be done in that regard. So we will stand in recess for an hour and a half for lunch. (12.35 p.m.) (Luncheon Adjournment) (2.00 p.m.) (Closed Session) – Confidentiality lifted by Trial Chamber II on 29.07.96

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are now in closed session and I will ask the audio visual director to confirm that this proceeding at this point is not being released to the media at this time? Very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution will call witness H, your Honour. WITNESS H, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will ask that the witness please take the oath that is being handed to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. (The witness was sworn)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. H, you were born in 1968?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three, three sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you born and raised in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you attend primary and secondary school in Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After your schooling did you work in the construction field?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you complete your compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you returned home from your compulsory military service, did you ever participate in any reserve training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of a TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever participate in politics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you work out of the Kozarac area for several years before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you return home on weekends and holidays?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know a man named Dusko Tadic from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him from Kozarac, from the town, and when I trained for one year karate and he was my instructor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know his wife's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mira.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know whether his wife worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the hospital in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In addition to training for a year in karate, did you ever see the man you know, Dusko Tadic, around the village of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know what he did for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that. I know that he trained karate. Maybe he made money from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Before the war had you ever seen the man Dusko Tadic with a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Had you seen him on occasions without a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you at home in the Kozarac area when the attack on that area started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did that attack start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May 24th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 2.15 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How did the attack start, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, the shelling started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When the shelling began what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I got scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you leave your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know where to go and what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So where did you end up going first?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the next village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the next village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you return home the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you do at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. I was with the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you stay at your home for the rest of the time during the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What would you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We ran all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why were you running all over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there was shooting from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At some point did you go to the village of Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sivci, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Tuesday evening, the whole night and then early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why did you leave Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because it also started there, the shooting and grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left Sivci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you captured at your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you explain how you were eventually captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We returned that morning with the family, and some of our neighbours with a tractor and a trailer, the wife and children. We came home and we found the cattle, the livestock, outside. Then we tied them, then we fed it, then had lunch and then we bathed and we did the laundry, and then we were at home until again the shelling started and the ordnance started falling in the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you do when that happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then I fled to a crevice, to a ravine, with my wife and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was in this ravine that you fled to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a very small ravine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there a stream in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were in that ravine what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
