utterances.text: I heard some noise, and I went over to see what it was about. I left the child. I turned it over to either my mother or my wife and started uphill to a point where I could have a good view of what the noise was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you see when you got up there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a column of people, my neighbours and one soldier who was escorting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did your neighbour saying anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the soldiers beckoned to me and they also shouted that we were going to some kind of a meeting. I agreed to come along and I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there, in fact, any meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did this group of people you were with, the soldiers, eventually make your way to the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you got to the entrance of Kozarac, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a lot of military there, and more people, civilians, our civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were the military that you mentioned saying anything to the people you were with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were they saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They cursed us, our balija mothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of this group of civilians that you were with, the ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hardly. They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were in Kozarac where was your group taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor. We came to Limenka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is Limenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a bus stop that was called Limenka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was it on the Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that the new road or the old road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: New, the new road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at Limenka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There we were separated, women and children from men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened to the men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were separated out down the hill on the other side of the road and they searched us, and the women and children remained on the other side, the upper side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did the Serb soldiers say anything to you, any of the male prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we started climbing on to the buses a man was walking next to me, and a soldier stopped him and asked him how many Serbs he killed, and he remained behind and I went on to the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you got on the bus, what happened after you were on the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got into the buses and started towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did the buses end up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened to you once the buses arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were brought to the grounds, to the enclosure, those buses, and waited for sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long did you wait in those buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What time of the day was it now when you arrived at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you got off the buses was it still afternoon or was it now evening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At dusk, it was not night yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened when you got off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The soldier escorting us told us to -- for us from that village to stand aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The soldier you are referring to, is that the same soldier who had escorted your group from your village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you mention he told those of you from that village, do you mean that group that you had been in, that same group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly, we were mostly from that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So that guard was separating you out from the others on the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he said that we should step aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened when he told you to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People began to join us, and then he returned and indicated back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When the guard returned, you say he "indicated back", what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On to the bus again, all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How was he acting when he came back and saw that the group had not been separated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was agitated, angry, and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why do you think the other prisoners who had not been originally part of your group tried to join with your group when the guard had told you to be separated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know. They probably thought it meant some ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Had that guard who had escorted you treated your group differently than some of the other guards had treated other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He behaved quite all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Once you were all told to get back on the buses, where did the buses go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A column was formed, whether it was around midnight or after midnight, I would not know, and we were taken somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did the buses finally stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Once you arrived at Omarska what occurred when you first got off the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They forced us to run off the buses and there were soldiers lined up on both sides along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened when you ran between those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those soldiers hit us, they kicked us with their hands or with their rifle butts as long as we were running between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you put in a building after you ran through that cordon of guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which building was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We ran through a door, then we went up the stairs, right, right and then right again to a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. H, at this point could you please stand and using the pointer move around to the model and using the pointer would you please indicate the room that you were placed in when you first arrived at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to stand in front of the witness desk?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Ma'am, he is aware.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be switched on for the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. H, when you speak you are going to need to ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From somewhere here there was a path to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Can we have the camera switched on, please? OK. It is on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Yes, please, could you indicate where you were taken out of the buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bus stopped somewhere here, and this part we had to run across between those guards who hit us, to this door here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then up the stairs, and to which room were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up the stairs to the left. We went then to the right and then to the right to a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Could you point to that room, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the model).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you identify which room you are pointing to by the letter and number designator that is in there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I notice that in that area of the room B7 there also would appear to be two smaller rooms. Do you know what was in those smaller areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some tin wash basins or tubs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did the prisoners who were in the camp consider that entire area, including those two smaller rooms, to be one single room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could return to your seat? How many days did you end up spending in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: During the first few days, two or three days, were you allowed out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only if someone had to go to the WC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How crowded was that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was overcrowded. There were very many people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there enough space for each person to be able to lay down and sleep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no room to sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did you receive your first meal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How did you feel after those first three days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Scared, hungry, complete uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were people being taken out for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How were people called out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did you go for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the fifth or sixth day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A soldier came, and it was that everyone had to go for interrogation and I decided to go. I was taken to a room, the kitchen where the restaurant was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What part of that building were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken into the building, up the stairs, and up there when I mounted the stairs, there was a soldier standing to the left side on the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you taken into a separate room for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of questions were you asked during the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether I had any money, whether I had a rifle, to empty my pockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Any other types of questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afterwards there was where I worked, what did I do, how did I travel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you beaten during your interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you know who your interrogator was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of clothes was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After the interrogation was over where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was returned back to the same building, but downstairs in the ground, on the ground floor. I did not go back to where I had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could please again approach the model and point to the room where you were taken after interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you returned where were you taken, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We entered here, through this door, crossed this here in this room. This is where I was brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could please use the pointer again and indicate inside the room, point to the inside of the room, please? Could you identify that room by the letter and number designator, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In that room did you go upstairs or did you remain on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all full already so I stayed close to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat, Mr. H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Would you ask the witness, are those glass doors?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am going to get to that right now. If I could have this photograph marked as the next Exhibit in order which is 261 and then hand it to the witness, please? I am going to need the Elmo. Mr. H, do you recognise that picture, Exhibit 261?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the Elmo, please? Thank you. What is that picture, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the room in which I was, where I was brought after the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could we have the lights dimmed, please, while this picture is on the Exhibit? I guess not. Is this photograph taken from the landing of the stairway down into the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the landing at the top of the stairs downward, to the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is different in this picture from when you were in the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The metal lockers on both sides are gone and this was not here, these boots, these hammers and these clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you could indicate, please, with the pointer generally the area where you spent your time in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The witness indicated on the picture) About here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So as we look at that picture it would be on the left side where the wheelbarrow is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated there were lockers along the walls in that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you on the floor or on the lockers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the floor -- on the tiles, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So would your back have been up against the locker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer Exhibit 261, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you find out from the witness what sort of lockers these were, what are their shape?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It is coming up, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no objection but we would like a copy of it which we have not been supplied with.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 261 will be admitted. Please provide the Defence with a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I believe they have been provided with a black and white copy but not a colour copy yet. If we could next bring up on the computer picture No. 18-15? (To the witness): Mr. H, you see the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There are lockers on the left-hand side of that picture as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were tin lockers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are those similar to the lockers which lined the walls of the room in which you stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would offer that Exhibit as No. 262.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour, but please may we have a copy as well?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 262 will be admitted. Provide them with a colour copy ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- of both, 261 and 262.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could now have photograph 58-12 brought up on the computer, please? (To the witness): Mr. H, do you see the photograph in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise what that is, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The door to the room in which I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This photograph was taken from the garage area looking at the doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would offer this photograph as the next Exhibit No. 263.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour, but please may we have a copy as well?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I was going to ask can that be marked and handed to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 263 will be admitted and a copy will be provided to the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is my understanding that they have black and white copies now. We are in the process of trying to get colour copies, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It is my mistake, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you need to hold on to the Court's copy of 261 and 262 at this point? You may, if the Registrar will allow that, if they are not being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To ensure that, the question raised by Judge Stephen, could Exhibit 260 -- actually it is a photograph, it looks like 1924, if that could be brought up, please, which I believe is Exhibit 260? (To the witness): Do you recognise that picture, Exhibit 260, Mr. H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Those are the doors to the room in which you stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: While we are being architectural, would it be possible through this witness or somebody else to explain these canals that are always referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It will be coming up, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: While we are being architectural, it would be helpful to me for the witness to give me an estimate of the height of the bottom panel on these doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Witness H, do you see in the photograph the metal at the bottom of the doors, the bottom panel which is painted red?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall and can you approximate about how tall the panel was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, about 40 centimetres, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. How full was that part of the room where you stayed at the bottom of the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was filled to capacity. I looked for a place somewhere further away from the door, but I could not find it. There were people already on top of the lockers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were sitting on the floor, was there room for you to spread your things out and for you to spread out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At night we would lie down, we stretched our legs one across the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The people who were on top of the lockers, did they have to sleep up there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were there all the time, both day and night.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What about the stairs, were the prisoners on all of the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Full, everything was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What about the room at the top of the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Upstairs likewise, everything full.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In that room that you were in, the downstairs and then the stairway and the area at the top of the stairs, the room at the top, was that whole area considered one room by the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So both the ground floor and the upstairs were considered part of the same room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was each prisoner's space recognise as belonging to that prisoner? In other words, if a prisoner left the area, could they return to their own space?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Everyone knew where his place was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The other prisoners would respect that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had to -- there was nothing else to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were there ever guards posted as a regular guard post upstairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, inside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of all of the prisoners in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly Muslims and there were some Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would like to show you a series of photographs and ask you if you can identify any of the people. I would like this marked as one exhibit, 264 and then A through K, please? Copies of these have been provided to the Defence, your Honour. I will need the Elmo. (To the witness): Mr. H, what I would like you to do, please, is to look at each photo and place it on the Elmo and indicate if you recognise any of those people and what their names are.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I gather that is A?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this young man, Sakib Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would ask the record to reflect that he is pointing to the young man who is basically in the centre of the picture, appears to be wearing some type of sweater, jacket, with a red and white stripe.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, the record will so reflect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, and B? If you could lower the lights again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Bahunjic and the first one is Grozdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The first name mentioned would be the second man in the picture in the line. Thank you. And C -- excuse me, were both those men in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, we wish to enquire where you are going with this testimony, I suppose, and 50 minutes now almost -- I think we began at 2.15 -- is this relevant and, if so, are you going to tie it up with something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You mean this particular naming of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We believe it is relevant to what is most likely to be a required element of proving that if there was a widespread and systematic attack it was against a particular civilian population. This is evidence to go to affirm that element.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So he is going to identify by the names and then their religion?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Correct, and where they are from generally.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, move along. I have not heard anything in 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We have already heard endlessly that there were Muslims with, perhaps, a few Croats. Do you want more than that? Do you really want 20 or 30 names? Is that going to do any good -- names which mean nothing to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Except that as opposed to saying that generally they were Muslims in the camp, it was our feeling that it might be helpful to be able to actually pin point that, have them specifically identified, individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What you might do, you have A through K -- of course, we are taking time discussing this and you try the case any way you want -- and there are pictures of numerous people. I guess he is going to identify them. Ask him if he has looked at those pictures, does he know the individuals in those pictures and then ask what is their ethnicity or religion. Depending upon cross-examination, that may not even be challenged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If it is challenged, then you can come back and we can spend 20 minutes and we can go through and name all of them. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Mr. H, if you would, please, look through the rest of the series of photographs, simply look at each photograph in the pile.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a Croat, there is one Croat on this picture and then Sefer and Emir and Mujo, Jakupovic, a young man of 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If you would just look through the rest of the pictures first. Did you recognise some or all of the people in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have, I have.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How many did you recognise and what is their religion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps not all of them but most, mostly they are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How many people would you estimate, from looking at this stack of pictures, 264A through K, did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At least 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were those pictures taken at Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Finished, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would tender that Exhibit now, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 264A through K will be admitted. Do not get upset, Mr. Keegan. Really, I have heard almost 55 minutes of testimony; I have not heard a thing really that helps me at all with any of the issues in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection to the Exhibits, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted. 264A through K. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): From that room where you were sitting, Mr. H, on occasion did you witness any beatings of any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was inside two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: First, did you observe the beatings of prisoners out in the hangar area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What do you mean you could not look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While they are beating, especially if it is right in front of you, a metre away, you just drop your head down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What would happen if you were caught looking while someone was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they would beat me too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever witness someone in your room being beaten for exactly that, having been caught watching someone else being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you witness the death of any prisoners in your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw when they brought back the President of HDZ from interrogation and he succumbed from the wounds he sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He was the President of the HDZ Party from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor, from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the day of the incident that you were forced to take part in, what is the first thing that you remember happening that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were playing music too loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of music was being played?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly it was those Serb nationalist songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What else was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then you could hear, as they beat some people outside, you could hear noises of different objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was going on inside the rooms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People were -- people got upset, they were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did they do or try to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly what one, the best one could do was to get away from the door, not to be close there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So where were people trying to go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were many successful in doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those around the door, yes, they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you manage to get up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the next thing that you recall happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember when they called out people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who do you remember being called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember Emir Karabasic, Jasmin Hrnic, Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If I could have this photograph marked as the next exhibit, please? It will be Exhibit 265. (To the witness): Mr. H, do you recognise the people in that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you point to those people and indicate their names, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This man is called, his name is Jasmin Hrnic and the man next to him is Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can the record reflect that the man indicated as Jasmin Hrnic as the tall man on the extreme right hand side of the picture and Emir Karabasic is the man immediately to his left, a shorter man, who appears to be in a black coat, shirt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would offer 265, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 265 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. H, what do you remember about when Jasmin Hrnic was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that he was called out. First they said "Asko Hrnic" several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, the translation of your answer says: "First they called out Jasko Hrnic", is that what they said, "Jasko"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Asko Hrnic, first it was Asko Hrnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK, beginning with an "A", A-S-K-O, Asko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And that is how it remained, they kept calling Asko until he responded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know where Jasmin Hrnic was in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was right below where I was, the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. When you say "below", do you mean in the room next to yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not the first next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So two rooms away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was our room and then sort of below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What do you remember about Eno Alic being called out? How was he called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His father came for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did they have to go past you on the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First Meho passed alone, and then he returned with Eno.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you see any of the soldiers who called these prisoners out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You could see, but very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which guard could you see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one that was calling out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Calling out who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Asko, Jasko Hrnic that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What type of uniform did that man have on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a blue shirt on and police trousers and white belt around those trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that man in the camp before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing him in the camp after this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After the three men were called out, Jasmin Hrnic, Emir Karabasic and Eno Alic, could you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard inside in the room human wails as they screamed out and then you could hear the blows, the noises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What could you hear them screaming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They just screamed very loud, "My mother, don't beat me, why are you beating me?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you hear the prisoners being ordered to do anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard that they were forcing someone to eat a pigeon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are about to get into a point in the testimony where the witness is going to talk about his particular participation. I would rather do it in one sequence. I am happy to either continue on -- it should take 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We had planned on recessing, I suppose, at 3.45 since we started at a different time today because of the lunch. Is that acceptable to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That is fine, your Honour. I just was not sure because of the different schedule. I did not want it broken.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: At 3.45 we will recess. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Mr. H, at some point were you and Mr. G called out of your room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How did that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that the noise, the beating abated somewhat and one of the guards, a young man, came and called for two men to take some men out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you see this guard who came and called out for two volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was young and he was trembling with fear, in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise him as a regular guard in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did anybody respond to his order for two volunteers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody, nobody stepped out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then somebody, a bearded person, came and shouted and said, "You and you".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I probably looked at him at that moment and then he called me out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. H, if you could please go again to the model for the next few questions? Mr. H, after you left your room which way did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the room to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the first thing that you noticed when you left the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot of blood, puddles of blood, all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you came out of the room where were you looking? Were you looking around the garage area or where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you saw the blood what was the next thing that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw the body of Emir Karabasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With the pointer can you indicate generally where you saw that body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That was generally as we look at the model between the canals Z and Y, close to the canal marked Z?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you just indicate in which direction was the head of Emir Karabasic pointing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This direction here, in the direction of WC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. For the record, that would be in the direction on the model of the building, the administration building, in that direction on the model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Once you saw Emir's body what then happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then somebody asked, "Whom are we going to take? What do we have to do? Who is it?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was there an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "Come over here".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you have to go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again in the direction of the toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you go to? What spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We passed by this canal here and we stopped here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which canal is that, which letter, canal Y?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Y.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With the pointer, if you could indicate what you saw when you got to that canal and where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Let the record reflect the witness is pointing adjacent to the letter designated the piece of paper Y?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you see when you got to that spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two more bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you recognise the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one was Jasmin Hrnic and the other body was Eno Alic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were those bodies positioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: For the record, in what direction were the heads of those bodies pointing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of this large garage door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were the bodies next to the canal marked Y?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Whose body was closest to the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jasmin's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You can return to your seat, Mr. H. When you reached the area next to canal Y where the bodies were, what were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To carry Eno Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you get a look at the man who ordered you to pick up the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you describe that man, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a military uniform on, a green one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he tall or short?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Medium height, neither short nor tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did he have light hair or dark hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that the man who had picked you to come out of the room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you tried to pick up Eno's body what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to pick him up under his arms and he was slipping, slipping out. He was still alive and he was fighting back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So what happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then that man put his foot on Eno's throat, on Eno's neck, and was pushing it up and down, so that his head was turning backwards and forwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated the man put his foot on Eno's throat and neck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, Jasmin's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So it was Jasmin's head that turned backwards and forwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told to carry him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you pick him up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we were again told, ordered, to grab him one by one foot and another one by the other foot and to drag him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were you to drag him to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out of that garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you drag him down to the garage door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that garage door open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers around in the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know where they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were also some inside the garage and out of it and in the doorway. They were moving about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you looking around in the garage and looking at these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only in so far as I could while we went up and down trying to pick up and drag Jasmin's body just for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you brought Jasmin's body to the door, what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To take him back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Back to where you had picked him up from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you forced to repeat this a couple of times, back and forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There between this back and forth, somewhere midway, they told us to let him go, and to lie down and stand up, to do push ups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you say somewhere midway told you to let him go, would that be midway along canal Y?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you did this lie down, stand up and push ups, what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Come to the canal, to the edge of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If I could have photograph 18-2 brought up, please, on the computer? Mr. H, do you see that picture in front of you on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a mechanical canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that a picture of a canal like the one that you now are describing in your evidence, canal Y?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This one is nearer to this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: But were the canals basically identical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If I could have this handed to the Registrar and marked as 266, please, Exhibit 266, and then handed to the Bench? I would offer Exhibit 266, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 266 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could have picture 16-11 brought up, please? Mr. H, do you recognise that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that representative from the upstairs in the garage how the canals are situated in relation to the garage doors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that a picture of the canals inside the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I would offer 267, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 267 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Bos, if that could be handed to the Bench, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can you identify canal Y, just to locate ourselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I believe so, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. H, in this photograph would canal Y be the one that is on the right as you look at this photograph? It appears to have some type of screen on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In this photograph would canal Y, the canal we are talking about, be the canal on the right-hand side of the picture as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At the time that you were involved in this incident, that screen item that appears on the canal, was that there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: It is more like a trolley.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Actually when you look at the photograph, what it is, it is a grease trap, when they change the oil and they catch things. It is removable. (To the witness): When you were ordered to stand on the edge of the canal, what could you see in the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw oil and water in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you tell how deep that oil and water was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you thinking as you were standing there on the edge of that canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought it was deep, so deep that we would sink down and that they would push us down with their feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you jumped in how deep, in fact, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we jumped in it was a hard bottom and then I realised it was not, that it was not deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The whole canal itself, approximately, how deep is it? Where on your body did it come up to, the walls of the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was ordered immediately to lie down, perhaps up to here, when I jumped down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that witness indicated at about shoulder level.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: About?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Shoulder level, the neck.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I saw him touch his clavicle, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Clavicle, then fine, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know that it makes a significant difference. OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you were told to lie down, what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To lie down and crawl through that oil.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What end did you crawl to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was crawling, the first towards this large garage door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you got to the end, what were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To turn on our back and back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what were you ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To drink oil and water that were in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you drink that oil and water?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I just put my face down into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard him call, "Hari, come here".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And somebody came and jumped down in with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At the time did you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you later told what his name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the name you were told?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fikret Harambasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you know Fikret Harambasic before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why is it that you did not recognise him on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was all battered, bloody, black.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was he naked when he jumped into the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you ordered do at that time? Were you ordered to lick his arse, Mr. H?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. G ordered to suck his penis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the next order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was the next order for Mr. G to bite his testicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At that time what were the people around the canal yelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were yelling "Bite, harder, harder".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the next order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A knife was put against my eye, and I was ordered to hold his mouth with my hands and if they heard his voice they would gouge both my eyes, not only one, and the other one to go on biting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you first ordered to get out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why did he tell you to get out of the canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As if he could not see what was happening down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you got out of the canal what position were the three of you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My feet were against the big garage door and the two of them were there, more inside the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were all three of you laying down in a laying down position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You were closest to the garage door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Fikret Harambasic in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. G between Fikret Harambasic's legs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Is that when a knife was put against your eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you see or did you look at the person who put the knife against your eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so. I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was happening at that point after you were ordered to hold Fikret Harambasic's mouth closed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What happened after were you ordered to keep Fikret Harambasic's mouth closed, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then somebody put his foot on my neck and began to trample me, so that my chin was rubbing against the concrete and it got all sore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was Mr. G doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he was doing whatever he was being ordered to, whatever he was ordered to, he did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were they telling him to do at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To strike this one, to curse his Turkish mother for trying to fend off, to defend himself. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was Fikret Harambasic trying to cover himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did Mr. G do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He pulled his legs apart and his hands because he had his hands down on his genital, on his organ, and he was striking at him, cursing, as he had been told to, and went on doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At that time were people in the garage around you yelling things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were they yelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Look at them, mother, what they are doing to each other. Can you think what they would do to us if they are doing to each other this?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were there a lot of people in the garage yelling at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At one point did you say anything to Mr. G?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told him to stop, not to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did Fikret Harambasic say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was saying, "He's not normal, he really wants to do it".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then he implored them to kill him, Fikret did, with a rifle. He said, "Don't, kill me with a pistol. Don't torture me like that", he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he did and then pulled it out, his testicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. G bit off one of Fikret Harambasic's testicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Immediately after biting off the testicle, what did Mr. G do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He spit it out and that ball had fallen through the grate that was at this big garage door which served for sewage, to drain the water out, and it had fallen through and a vein or something stayed, got stuck in the grate and remained like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was Mr. G told after doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was free to go, that he could go inside now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What about you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I remained lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you then ordered to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told to drag him to the table, the desk that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was that table normally used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where the guards used to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After you dragged Fikret Harambasic over there, what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I pulled him up to that place, let him go and stood behind him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he asked me to get him water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What did you have to tell him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "I cannot bring it to you, I cannot move away from you".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And a soldier, one of these who had hit me with a rifle before while we were dragging him to and fro, he told me to get lost because they would kill me if I stayed there. That is what I did and I skipped upstairs.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes. (4.05 p.m.) (Short Adjournment) (4.25 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. There is a matter I want to raise before Mr. Keegan continues, that is, there is some confusion on our part since we changed not having the witness in a separate room with his image scrambled, voice scrambling, all that, but having him here, we thought the voice would be outside so people could follow what is going on here and, apparently, that is not the case. We thought that that was not exactly what we figured. I think the translation, there is no confusion if that would be broadcasted, there is no possible recognition whatsoever. So if the version in French and English will be broadcasted, people are able to follow.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is ESP. Mr. Wladimiroff, if I did not know that you could not have been with us, with the Judges (and you were not), we have been discussing the same matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: He probably would not know what "ESP" means.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Extra sensory perception, or whatever. We have been just discussing that very point. Thank you. Let me hear what Mr. Keegan has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We understood that it was going to be a closed session, but we would be happy to have an accelerated release of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The point, and the reason that motivated our discussion, was a desire, in principle, to have these proceedings as open as is possible, because (1) the accused is entitled to a public trial, and (2) the public may have some interest and in some national systems there is a right on the part of the public to have access, in some national systems. Of course, we do not have that in our Rules, but the accused is entitled to a public trial, and that component is going out. If you have no objection, I presume we can make an arrangement to have just the voice, just the testimony go out, but again with no image, with no image of the witness testifying. There has been no French translation, but Miss Featherstone says that can be done. Fine. We will make the necessary arrangements to assure that the audio of the testimony is released to the public as soon as we can have a French translation as well, but otherwise the protections will remain as is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That would be only the English and the French translation -- the translations basically, not the witness's original statement voice because he is an anonymous witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He did ask for voice alteration originally?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Originally, but his agreement working in the courtroom was he agreed to waive that, but that was in terms of all of the people present in the courtroom, not release to the general public. So if, in fact, the only thing released is the interpreters's voice, that is fine, then there is no disclosure. That is the only point I am trying to make clear.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is what we were thinking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is exactly what we are thinking about too but, your Honour, would there be a problem not having a French interpreter but starting with the English who are available?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It would not be a problem with me, but my French colleagues in the Tribunal might have a problem with me doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, just to be clear, as I may be a little confused, we are talking about not simultaneous broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, it will all be delayed, our delayed procedures, half hour delay, as well as with the redaction, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: I think that is only available in connection with the video recording and not in the connection with the audio channels. Maybe we should ask Gert Jan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Because again he is an anonymous witness with full protection, I would be very concerned about -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What we can do in an effort to let the public know is to complete, at least, the direct and the cross-examination. We will then have the audio. We will then release it after the parties have had an opportunity to review the audio, to assure that there have been no slips. That can be done very quickly, perhaps today, so then we would have the audio. That would only be the audio in English. I do not know how we would then be able to get the translators to then listen to it and do the translation. I imagine that would take the same amount of time that we heard his testimony -- no?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You would have to produce a whole new audio record.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am the one who always believes that there is a solution to everything. If the desire of both parties is to have the audio released in English and French, but at the same time protecting the voice of the witness, we will endeavour to talk with the technical people and see how and whether it can be done. Is that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, that is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before we take any decision, we will tell you exactly how it will be done. We would do that this evening and advise you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is the best we can do, Mr. Wladimiroff, unless you can help me in some other regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have a little preference in having the English broadcasted. I would say that the right of the public to know, as you described, is of a different standard than I do accept more or less a sensible feeling of one of the Judges about the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It is not just the Judges; the French Foreign Minister has strong views and so has the whole French nation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Absolutely, your Honour, but so far I have found that since my French is not that excellent, everyone I spoke to in the context of this Tribunal, French or not, they all speak English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: But they do not admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is not the point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will get it done, Mr. Wladimiroff, I really will -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May I raise just in the context of this, I also learned that having transcripts for the public is quite a difficult issue. Whether that is true or not, I have been told it will take up to three months before you will have that. That is in the context we are talking now also a problem I may draw your attention to.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The transcript situation -- I do not know whether it is three months. I think I would like to be proud of our Trial Chamber. I think that we do a pretty good job. I do not know about three months, though, but excuse me one minute. Mr. Wladimiroff, what I am told is that we do not have a three month delay, at least this Trial Chamber. It takes approximately a week but, on the safe side, a week to 10 days. To go from the transcript that we get after this proceeding, it is then looked at to correct any errors and then after that the clean copy or the final copy is prepared and the Registry usually has that in a week. The Registry then has the transcripts and then the Registry makes the determination about their dissemination. Have you been having a problem getting the final?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We do not have a problem at all. I am just passing to you what we have heard from people from the audience. If there is no sound, no image and also not a transcript available, you see, that is the context why I brought this message to you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I appreciate that. I will check into that, perhaps talk with Mr. Chartier since he would have the contact with some of those people in the audience. By tomorrow morning we will tell you what can be done technically to achieve this purpose, to reach this purpose, reach this solution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know. We just have to talk to a couple of people and see if it can be accomplished, but it is our desire also for as much as possible to go out. OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We appreciate your efforts.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: For the record, I should make a statement -- I did not want to interrupt Mr. Keegan -- by a majority decision of the Trial Chamber the accused, who is in the court and has been in the court from the beginning of the testimony of witness H, has not been viewing the witness while the witness is testifying, but the accused is hearing his testimony. The accused’s counsel and the Judges and the Prosecution can both see and hear witness H while he is testifying. So I just wanted to read that into the record, particularly if there was going to be a question about, now there may not be a question about the audio, but only we would know what was happening and so I wanted to make that statement. Mr. Keegan, would you like to continue with direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. H, from the time that you were told to put down the body of Jasmin Hrnic and go to the canal and through the rest of the incident, did you look around the room to try to identify who else was in that garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you focus your gaze, if you will, where did you look, during the time you were out in that garage area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What were you afraid would happen if you were caught looking around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought that if anyone would see me looking at them that I would not fare very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You testified that it was the man with the beard whom you described earlier who gave you the order to carry the bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After the time that you were ordered to jump into the canal and for the rest of the incident, do you know for certain who was giving you orders? Did you ever look to see who was giving you orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not dare look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have generally any idea of how many people were in that garage? How many Serb guards or soldiers were in that garage during this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: From what you could tell, were those people, those soldiers, those guards, the ones who were doing the yelling and screaming during the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you see Dusko Tadic in the garage that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When did you leave Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On August 6th we left Omarska and the next day we went to ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you repeat where you went to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On August 6th we left Omarska and on the 7th we entered through the fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To what camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How long were you in Manjaca camp for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 7th to December 14th the same year, '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I know we are concluding at 5 o'clock this evening, are we?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We do have another matter at 5.30, I guess. How long do you estimate for cross, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I estimate that it will be somewhere towards 25 minutes to half an hour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us see if we can finish then, but you take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
