utterances.text: Mr. H, as you told the Court, you knew Dusko Tadic as a man who lived in Kozarac, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The place that you lived, was that part of Kozarac? Am I saying something -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might, part of the anonymity, of course, is anything that might give away the identity. As the Court knows, some of these villages are very small and it might be very easy, which is why I referred to Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In the report that you have given the Defence regarding witness H, was there some mention of that, where he lived?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I do not have the statement in front of me, but it should have been redacted, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me see. The witness has already testified that he knew Mr. Tadic and that he took lessons for a while, karate lessons. I suppose that does not mean that he had to live in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He admits to living in the Kozarac area, your Honour. My fear is that if he names the village, it is going to make it very easy to identify who the witness is. That is my concern.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. The question has gone. What was the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was an obvious place for me to start at and perhaps I can circle around in a different way. I apologise for entering territory that we did not want. (To the witness): If I can start again, Mr. H: It would be fair to say that you knew Kozarac area well, it was your local area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You gave a description of seeing Dusko Tadic on occasions with a beard and without a beard, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you had seen his appearance in two forms during the time that you had known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were in Omarska you spent your time in this area which is a hallway beneath the stairs, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the door and not under the staircase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Excuse me, if could I have that relayed back to me as I was put on to a different channel?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please play that back or repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Repeat it verbally? "Next to the door and not underneath the staircase".

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, your Honour, lost my channel.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It should be 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it can get knocked. (To the witness): In that part of the building where you were confined, were there other people from your region also held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you able to go upstairs to the place upstairs where people were also held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no room for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As I understand it from the model that we have seen, there is, in fact, a long corridor at the top of the stairs which then leads to a bigger room, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But that was all filled with people, one person on top of the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever have the opportunity to go up the stairs and see the rooms there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the incident I had I went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you went up those stairs did you go down the corridor to a large room at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went through the door and went up the stairs over people and I stepped over somebody's head or foot or hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that the first time that you had been upstairs during your stay in this part of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember about how many days you had been held in this place before this incident happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember how many days later it was before you left Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere midway, somewhere in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. On this occasion when you and the man we call G were selected to leave that area at the bottom of the stairs, it was a man with a beard who came and told you to come out of the room, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A military uniform, a green one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that be a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. SMB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: SMB, the old style army uniform, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an old expression from that army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. At that stage you left that room and went out into the hangar and there you noticed the bodies that you indicated to us, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was the man with the beard who took you out of that room on his own or was he with someone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were near him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how far away were the other soldiers who were in the hangar? Were they grouped anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: More grouped but they moved about, they moved around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect which part of the hangar they were, generally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the big garage doors, a little bit inside and then outside of the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, they were down at the other end of the garage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is all closed but they were at the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What exactly were those soldiers doing? I am asking this from the time that you first entered the hangar, having left your room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw a group. I did not see what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You saw Emir Karabasic's body by one of the canals and were you shown that or did you happen to see it as you moved through the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have to do anything with that body or did you just walk past it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just passed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time the man called G was with you as well, you were together, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Still with the man with the beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he taking you then to the position of the other two bodies where Jasko Hrnic and Eno Alic lay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He asked us to come there and he was leading us and we were following.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He took you to the place where those two bodies were, and gave you orders in respect of one of those bodies, the body of Eno Alic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, he gave you an order in relation to the body of Eno Alic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to carry him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So he was talking to you and you were having to listen to his instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The body that you actually had to drag around, that was the body of Jasmin Hrnic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us about going up the garage to the doors and back again because another guard told you to take it away, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, I thought that is what I understood. Perhaps you can tell us. You were ordered to take the body up the garage, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you had taken the body up the garage, what happened then with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were ordered again to bring it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So did you take the body back to where you had originally ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exactly. Somewhere around midway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the two of you carrying the body between you, one with the legs and the other with the top part of the body or were you dragging it on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragging it on the ground by its legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The man with the beard, he had been the one who told you to take it up the garage, but did he say where to and what you should do with the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How many times did that happen that you went up the garage with the body and down again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whilst you were doing that, no doubt you were able to notice the soldiers who were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that panic, on that fear, I do not know how much I could notice, and one even hit me with a rifle butt as I was going back and forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Those soldiers who were there, were there guards who were part of the regular guards of the camp also at this place at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a lot of them, there were guards. I knew the guards, as much as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know if those guards were guards from a particular shift, Krkan's shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were Krkan's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So you were familiar with the guards who were part of each particular shift, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember which of the guards from Krkan's shift were there at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember the best this Bakal who was close to us all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that Bakal spelt B-A-K-A-L?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with a scar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A scar on his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember any of the other guards from Krkan's shift who were there at this time by name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you did not know them by name, you were just familiar with them as being part of that shift, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I knew faces but not names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that you looked at this man with the beard a few times when he was giving you your orders, and you would also be able to see those other people who were around him at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was all just for a moment, very briefly, in this panic, this fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You, presumably, could not see everyone who was in the room but some of them you could, would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This Bakal was close. He stayed in my mind best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But one thing is sure, that the man with the beard giving you orders was not Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You never saw Dusko Tadic in Omarska, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The last time you had seen Dusko Tadic he was wearing a beard, would that be right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long were you in the hangar during this incident? Can you remember how long the whole thing took from the time you entered and the time you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it was just before the shift change and they changed shifts at 7 o'clock, about an hour and a half before or two, I am not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were there involved in this incident for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The time that you were holding Fikret Harambasic's head, you had your feet against the garage door, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not against the door, just next to the door. The door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: G was down at the lower part of the man's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This time that he was biting the man's body, can you recollect how long that took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A long time, but I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Say some 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that stage were these guards and soldiers around watching what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that in a circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean they were in a circle and we were in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps you can explain how they were placed when they were watching what was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How could I know since I was lying down on my stomach?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you were obviously aware that they were there and this was something for their attention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard their voices, how merry they were. They were saying, "Look what you are doing to each other. Can you imagine what they would do to us?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you had to jump into the oil pit, again were they watching you? Was this some sort of entertainment for them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was down -- yes, I believe it was entertaining to them, but I was down in the canal, in the oil, in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When it had all finished you were allowed to go free. Was that the man with the beard who set you free or one of the other guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another one, it was another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that he was a guard on a shift but I do not know his name and his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You went through that door to your room and went to the level upstairs, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you were up there, were many people asking you because you were face to face with the man with the beard, if it was Dule, meaning Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did ask, they all asked what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they asking you if it was Dule, meaning Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You always told them that it was not him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You did not know who that man was with the beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just one moment. One question, Mr. H. When you described what happened after you got out of the canal and the three of you were laying down, earlier you described that Fikret Harambasic was struggling and that beating and force was having to be used. As a result of that, were the three of you moving, do you remember that, if that was the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were moving. We were moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. H, Mr. Kay just asked you if when you returned the persons who were in the room asked you whether it was Dule Tadic, and you answered that you did not know. Do you recall testifying to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not then, I did not see then that it was not him.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you returned to your room did the other prisoners ask you if it was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did more than one prisoner ask you if it was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a group of people who were there in that section by the WC where I had undressed and thrown off all my clothes and washed my hands a little, and others gave me some clothes, so it was a rather narrow circle of people who were around there. It was difficult to move about because there was no room for that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did they ask you if the person who did this, led you out, I guess, or had participated in this incident, did they ask you whether this was any other person by name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They asked me if it was Dule.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That was the only person's name they mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know why they would ask you whether it was Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You have probably testified to this but I do not recall, how many persons were in, if you can recall, this area of the hangar when G was forced to bite off the testicle of Mr. Harambasic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 20, 20. I would not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where were they located, if you can look at what is on your monitor? I do not know what Exhibit this is. Is it 267? Look at that picture on your monitor, where were these persons, if you can recall, positioned? We know that the canal with the screen, as it has been referred to, is Y, I think, is canal Y. Where were the soldiers and if there were guards involved where were they positioned? How far were they away from Y, canal Y?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that moment when I got out, I saw half of them in the garage at the big door and half of them were outside the garage. But where they were after that, where they moved about, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So was the garage door open then when the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You have referred to many of these people as "soldiers". By that did you mean that they were not the regular guards at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you refer to persons being "soldiers", by that did you mean that they were not the regular guards at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all of them. That one I had never seen before or after.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So some were the regular guards and some were persons who, as far as you knew, were not guards at Omarska camp, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to witness H being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Witness H, you are permanently excused. You are free to leave. Thank you very much for coming. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (5.30 p.m.) (The Court adjourned until the following day)
